haiku-low.q1: A PR runs build (not pushed) and unit tests only, never deploys. A merge to main starts the full pipeline that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production deploy the same image, registry.internal/shop-api:<commit SHA>, built once per run. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration failure gets one automatic retry; if it fails again, the run ends. Unit test failure has no retry and ends the run. Either way nothing reaches staging.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs the image it ran before this run. deploy.sh rollback staging restores it from SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers members who are not the commit author, within 72 hours. If no approval comes, the run expires, nothing reaches production, and staging keeps its image.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store under /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them, after a successful stable rollout or on rollback. The canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Stable deployment is untouched, SSM tags are unchanged, and the schema stays migrated (migrations are not reverted). The canary is turned off.
haiku-low.q8: It is cancelled as superseded and posts a notice to #deploys. This applies to runs waiting for approval, the window, or the lock.
haiku-low.q9: It waits and re-checks every 5 minutes until inside Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC with the production lock free. Approvals do not expire.
haiku-low.q10: Measured: canary 5xx ratio from Prometheus. The canary-watch step queries every 60 seconds for 15 minutes. One reading above 1%, or no data, fails it at once.
haiku-low.q11: The run posts to #deploys with IMAGE_TAG, a link to smoke results, and commits between production current_tag and IMAGE_TAG.
haiku-low.q12: Staging: kubectl rollout undo returns to the pods that were running, since SSM still names them; rollback would go one version too far back. Production: kubectl rollout undo, then canary-off; the reason for production is NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: A pull request runs build (image not pushed) and unit tests only, posting a status on the PR; it never deploys. A merge to main starts the full pipeline.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the same image registry.internal/shop-api:<commit SHA> (IMAGE_TAG), built once per run. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure gets one automatic retry; if the retry also fails, the run fails. A unit test failure gets no retry and fails the run immediately. Any final failure ends the run, posts the failing step to #deploys, and nothing reaches staging.
sonnet.q4: Staging runs the image it ran before this run. deploy.sh rollback staging sets current_tag back to SSM previous_tag (the image staging ran before this run).
sonnet.q5: A member of release-approvers who is not the commit author, approving in the CI UI. If no approval within 72 hours (clock starts at the gate), the run ends as expired, a notice goes to #deploys, nothing goes to production, and staging keeps the image.
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store, outside the pipeline, at /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them: after a successful stable rollout (deploy.sh <env> <tag>), and on rollback (current_tag set back to previous_tag). The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment untouched, SSM tags unchanged, and the schema stays migrated (migrations are not reverted). deploy.sh canary-off removes the canary.
sonnet.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded (whether waiting for approval, window or lock) and posts a notice to #deploys, provided it has not started its production deploy.
sonnet.q9: It waits and re-checks every 5 minutes until the time is inside the start window (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC) and the production lock is free. The approval does not expire (e.g. Thursday evening approval starts Monday 09:00).
sonnet.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio is measured. The canary-watch step queries Prometheus every 60 seconds for 15 minutes. Failure is any single reading above 1% or a query returning no data, which fails it at once and triggers canary-off.
sonnet.q11: The run posts a waiting-for-approval notice to the #deploys channel with IMAGE_TAG, a link to the smoke results, and the commits between production current_tag and IMAGE_TAG.
sonnet.q12: Staging and production both use kubectl rollout undo (production then also runs canary-off), which returns to the pods that were running. Not deploy.sh rollback in staging because SSM was not written, so it still names the old image, and previous_tag would go one version too far back. (Document gives this reason explicitly only for staging.)
